# CloudGraph rules

<!-- Generated by `cloudgraph rules --format markdown`. Do not edit by hand. -->

41 rules. Findings feed the attack path engine; most of them come with a virtual fix for the what-if simulator.

## Docker Compose

| ID | Severity | Rule | Remediation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CG-DC-001` | critical | Privileged container | Remove `privileged: true`. Grant only the specific capabilities the service needs with cap_add. |
| `CG-DC-002` | critical | Container runtime socket mounted | Do not mount docker.sock into application containers. Use a socket proxy with a read-only API allow-list if access is unavoidable. |
| `CG-DC-003` | high | Sensitive host path mounted | Mount named volumes or narrow, read-only subdirectories instead of system paths such as /, /etc or /proc. |
| `CG-DC-004` | medium | Host network namespace | Remove `network_mode: host` and publish only the ports that are needed. |
| `CG-DC-005` | high | Host PID / IPC namespace | Remove `pid: host` and `ipc: host`. |
| `CG-DC-006` | high | Dangerous Linux capabilities added | Drop ALL capabilities and add back only what is required; never add SYS_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE or ALL. |
| `CG-DC-007` | high | Sensitive port published on all interfaces | Bind the port to 127.0.0.1 ("127.0.0.1:5432:5432") or drop `ports:` and use the internal Docker network. |
| `CG-DC-008` | high | Hard-coded secret in environment | Use Compose `secrets:` or reference a variable (`${DB_PASSWORD}`) supplied at deploy time; never commit literal credentials. |
| `CG-DC-009` | low | Unpinned image tag | Pin images to an explicit version or digest so deployments are reproducible and reviewable. |
| `CG-DC-010` | low | Container runs as root | Set `user: "10001:10001"` (or build the image with a non-root USER). |
| `CG-DC-011` | high | Seccomp / AppArmor confinement disabled | Remove `seccomp:unconfined` / `apparmor:unconfined` from security_opt. |

## Kubernetes

| ID | Severity | Rule | Remediation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CG-K8S-001` | critical | Privileged container | Set `securityContext.privileged: false` and grant only the specific capabilities required. |
| `CG-K8S-002` | medium | Privilege escalation not disabled | Set `securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`. |
| `CG-K8S-003` | medium | Container may run as root | Set `securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true` and a non-zero `runAsUser`. |
| `CG-K8S-004` | high | Sensitive hostPath volume | Avoid hostPath volumes; use emptyDir, PVCs or CSI drivers. Never mount the container runtime socket. |
| `CG-K8S-005` | high | Host namespaces shared with pod | Remove hostNetwork, hostPID and hostIPC unless the workload is a node-level agent. |
| `CG-K8S-006` | high | Dangerous capabilities added | Drop ALL capabilities and add back only what the process needs. |
| `CG-K8S-007` | low | Unpinned image tag | Pin images to a specific version or digest. |
| `CG-K8S-008` | low | No resource limits | Set `resources.limits` for CPU and memory to contain noisy-neighbour and DoS impact. |
| `CG-K8S-009` | medium | ServiceAccount token mounted into a pod with API permissions | Set `automountServiceAccountToken: false` on pods that do not call the Kubernetes API. |
| `CG-K8S-010` | critical | Wildcard RBAC permissions | Replace `*` with the explicit resources and verbs required. |
| `CG-K8S-011` | critical | Binding to cluster-admin | Bind workloads to purpose-built roles instead of cluster-admin. |
| `CG-K8S-012` | high | Role can read Secrets | Restrict `secrets` access to named secrets (resourceNames) or remove it; avoid list/watch which exposes all values. |
| `CG-K8S-013` | medium | Role can execute commands or create workloads | Remove pods/exec and workload create permissions from application roles; they allow lateral movement. |
| `CG-K8S-014` | high | Binding grants permissions to broad groups | Never bind roles to system:unauthenticated, system:authenticated or all ServiceAccounts. |
| `CG-K8S-015` | low | Workload not isolated by a NetworkPolicy | Add a default-deny ingress NetworkPolicy per namespace and allow only required flows. Enforcement requires a CNI that supports NetworkPolicy. |
| `CG-K8S-016` | medium | Ingress without TLS | Add a `spec.tls` section with a certificate secret (or let cert-manager issue one). |
| `CG-K8S-017` | info | Service exposed outside the cluster | Confirm the exposure is intended; prefer ClusterIP behind an authenticated Ingress. |
| `CG-K8S-018` | high | Hard-coded secret in environment | Reference a Secret with `valueFrom.secretKeyRef` (ideally synced from an external secret manager). |
| `CG-K8S-019` | high | Role can escalate privileges | Remove escalate, bind and impersonate verbs; they bypass RBAC's privilege-escalation prevention. |
| `CG-K8S-020` | low | Root filesystem is writable | Set `securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` and mount emptyDir volumes where writes are needed. |
| `CG-K8S-021` | medium | Secret manifest committed to configuration | Do not commit Secret manifests. Use sealed-secrets, SOPS or an external secrets operator. |

## Terraform (AWS)

| ID | Severity | Rule | Remediation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CG-TF-001` | critical | Security group open to the Internet on a sensitive port | Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, a bastion, or use SSM Session Manager instead of exposing management ports. |
| `CG-TF-002` | high | S3 bucket allows public access | Use a private ACL and enable all four S3 Public Access Block settings. |
| `CG-TF-003` | low | S3 bucket has no public access block in this plan | Add aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block (or enforce it at account level). |
| `CG-TF-005` | critical | IAM policy grants administrator access | Replace Action "*" / Resource "*" with the minimum set of actions and ARNs. |
| `CG-TF-006` | critical | RDS instance is publicly accessible | Set publicly_accessible = false and place the instance in private subnets. |
| `CG-TF-007` | medium | Storage is not encrypted | Enable storage_encrypted (RDS) / encrypted (EBS root volume) with a KMS key. |
| `CG-TF-008` | medium | Instance metadata service allows IMDSv1 | Set metadata_options { http_tokens = "required" } to enforce IMDSv2. |
| `CG-TF-010` | high | Role can escalate IAM privileges | Remove iam:PassRole / iam:Attach* / iam:Put* on Resource "*" or scope them to specific ARNs. |
| `CG-TF-011` | medium | Plaintext secret present in plan | Do not pass passwords or user_data secrets as literals; use manage_master_user_password, Secrets Manager or SSM. Plan and state files contain these values in clear text. |
